candidate_relations.label: Pheochromocytoma crisis
candidate_relations.reason: The reference requires both the pheochromocytoma etiology AND the resulting cardiomyopathy. 'Pheochromocytoma crisis' captures the adrenal tumor and its systemic crisis but does not specify the cardiomyopathy manifestation confirmed by apical ballooning on ventriculography.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the pheochromocytoma etiology but omits the cardiomyopathy component

candidate_relations.label: Apical Ballooning Syndrome
candidate_relations.reason: Apical ballooning syndrome (Takotsubo) is the cardiomyopathy component confirmed by ventriculography, but the reference specifically requires attribution to pheochromocytoma as the cause. Without the etiologic specification, this is incomplete.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the cardiac morphological/functional component but omits the pheochromocytoma etiology

candidate_relations.label: Acute Coronary Syndrome
candidate_relations.reason: Coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries, directly excluding obstructive ACS. The ST changes and troponin elevation are explained by pheochromocytoma-induced cardiomyopathy, not atherosclerotic coronary disease.

candidate_relations.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
candidate_relations.reason: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy is the cardiac component of the diagnosis supported by apical ballooning and normal coronaries, but the reference diagnosis specifically requires pheochromocytoma as the inducing cause, which this label omits.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies the cardiomyopathy type but omits the pheochromocytoma etiology

case_quality_flags: Reference diagnosis 'Pheochromocytoma-induced cardiomyopathy' is a composite requiring both etiologic (adrenal mass) and cardiac (Takotsubo/apical ballooning) components; no candidate captures both simultaneously.
